models.label: ECMWF IFS 0.25°
models.note: ECMWF's operational physics model, open-data release. Its gust field is a maximum over the output interval, not an instantaneous value, so gust factors look large in light air.

models.label: ECMWF AIFS
models.note: ECMWF's machine-learning model - a genuinely independent opinion. Publishes no gust field, so gusts come from IFS and ICON-2i only.

models.label: ItaliaMeteo ICON-2i
models.note: ItaliaMeteo / ARPAE high-resolution model for Italy - the finest grid available here. Runs only ~60-72 h ahead and updates every 12 h, so it drops out of the longer-range view.

models.label: Météo-France MFWAM
models.note: Full sea-state decomposition - total wave, wind wave and swell with heights, directions and periods.

models.label: ECMWF WAM 0.25°
models.note: Total significant wave height only - used to cross-check MFWAM.

briefing.headline: Light easterlies easing to near-calm through midweek — but the forecast ends 29 Sep, five days short of our 4 Oct start.
briefing.synopsis: The current pattern over the Aeolians is a slack, light-gradient regime: NE to E winds of roughly 6-12 kt at the outer islands early on 23 Sep (Panarea 12.4 kt from 057° at midnight, ECMWF IFS 0.25°/AIFS/ICON-2i consensus, 23 Sep 00Z-06Z runs), backing through N and dropping away overnight into 24 Sep, with most islands showing 1-4 kt by dawn. A weak W to NW sea-breeze signal reappears midday 25 Sep (Filicudi 8.6 kt from 264°). Seas fall in step — Filicudi 2.8 ft total wave on the morning of 23 Sep down to 0.3-0.8 ft by 25 Sep (MFWAM, 23 Sep 00Z, cross-checked by ECMWF WAM 0.25°). If a pattern like this held into October it would mean motor-sailing legs and easy overnight stops, but there is no basis in this data for expecting it to hold.
briefing.overnight_anchorage: For tonight, 23 Sep, the recommendation is Portorosa Marina — enclosed, all-round shelter, and the only listed option there, so the choice does not matter. Wind at Portorosa is 4.6 kt from 005° at 18:00 easing to 3.0 kt overnight, with 1.4 ft dropping to 1.0 ft wave (23 Sep 00Z consensus). Nothing in the payload would push the fleet to move. Note these are live dates for the dry run, not trip-date berthing.
briefing.tomorrow_morning: 24 Sep looks near-calm across the group: Lipari 2.1 kt from 299° at 06:00, Panarea 1.7 kt, Filicudi 1.1 kt, waves 0.6-0.8 ft (23 Sep 00Z consensus). Any departure window in that kind of air is limited by fuel and patience rather than weather. For the real trip, the 4 Oct departure window cannot be assessed yet — the model data runs only to 23:00 on 29 Sep.

cautions: None of the trip dates (4-8 Oct) are inside the forecast horizon, which ends 29 Sep. Treat every verdict above as a dry run against live weather, not a forecast for the passage.

Where models disagree by more than 6 kt the payload flags it: Lipari 06:00 on 23 Sep spans 2.4-10.5 kt, Stromboli same hour 4.2-10.3 kt, and 18:00 on 25 Sep at Portorosa 0.4-6.6 kt and Lipari 0.4-7.4 kt. Do not plan on the mean in those hours.
Gust figures from ECMWF IFS are interval maxima, so values like 27.2 kt at Filicudi against a 9.4 kt mean overstate what you will feel; treat them as a squall-potential flag only.
Marina del Gabbiano at Stromboli scores only workable (0.827) — open from every direction, shelter there depends entirely on it staying calm.
briefing.confidence_note: Confidence in the current-pattern description is reasonable — stability checks show mean wind shifts of only 0.5-1.3 kt out to 120 h — but for the trip dates themselves it is low to nil, since no model in this payload reaches past 29 Sep and mean direction shifts already run 52° at 72-120 h lead.
